title: Abu Simbel Sun Festival 2026: Dates & How to See It
meta_description: The Abu Simbel Sun Festival lights the temple's inner sanctuary on October 22, 2026. Here's how it works and how to plan the trip from Aswan.

image.alt: Sunrise lighting the facade of the Great Temple at Abu Simbel

body_html:
Twice a year, the sunrise lines up perfectly with the entrance of the Great Temple at Abu Simbel, sending light deep inside to the statues in its inner sanctuary. The next date is October 22, 2026. Here's what the Sun Festival is, why it happens, and how to plan the trip down from Aswan.

What Is the Abu Simbel Sun Festival?

The Sun Festival marks two mornings a year, around February 22 and October 22, when the first rays of sunrise travel through the entrance of the Great Temple and light up the statues of Ramses II, Amun-Ra and Ra-Horakhty in the inner sanctuary. Only the statue of Ptah, a god linked with the underworld, stays in shadow.

Ramses II had the temple cut into the sandstone cliff in the 13th century BC, and its orientation was planned so the sun would reach that far inside on these two mornings only. When the temples were moved to save them from Lake Nasser in the 1960s, the international engineering team rebuilding them made sure the alignment still works today.

When Is the Next Sun Festival?

The Sun Festival happens twice a year at Abu Simbel: around February 22 and October 22. The next date is October 22, 2026. Because the alignment depends on sunrise, visitors need to already be inside the temple at dawn, which means leaving Aswan hours earlier than a normal day trip.

How Do You Get to Abu Simbel From Aswan?

Abu Simbel sits about 280 km south of Aswan, a three to three-and-a-half hour drive through the desert on a well-maintained road. Regular day tours leave Aswan around 4:00 am to beat the heat and the crowds; for the Sun Festival, an even earlier private departure is needed to be inside the temple before sunrise.

  • Distance: about 280 km each way from Aswan.
  • Drive time: roughly 3 to 3.5 hours through the desert.
  • Normal departure: around 4:00 am for a standard day trip.
  • Festival-day departure: earlier still, arranged privately so you're seated before sunrise.

What Should You Book for the Sun Festival?

Our private Abu Simbel day tour from Aswan covers entry fees, a professional guide and private transport, from $100 per person by car or $90 by minivan, with the departure time adjusted so you reach the temple before sunrise. Because Sun Festival mornings draw large crowds, book a private departure well ahead of October 22.

Can You Combine the Sun Festival With a Nile Cruise?

Yes. Cruises that already include Abu Simbel, like the 3-night cruise from Aswan or the 4-night cruise from Luxor, can be timed around October 22 so the temple visit falls on the festival morning. Ask when booking so the itinerary lines up with the date.

Tips for Sun Festival Day

  • Go private, not shared: a private car or minivan lets you set the early departure time a shared bus can't.
  • Dress for a cold desert morning: pre-dawn temperatures drop well below the daytime heat, even in October.
  • Bring water and snacks: lunch isn't included by default, though a lunch box can be added when booking.
  • Arrive with time to spare: festival mornings are busier than a normal visit, so give yourself a buffer before sunrise.

Abu Simbel is usually paired with more time in the south. Read our Aswan guide for the rest of the city's temples and felucca sunsets, or our tips for visiting a Nubian village while you're in the area.

FAQs About the Abu Simbel Sun Festival

  • When exactly is the Abu Simbel Sun Festival in 2026?

    The alignment happens twice a year, and the next date is October 22, 2026. The same event repeats around February 22 each year.
  • Why does only one statue stay in the dark?

    The Great Temple's inner sanctuary holds four seated statues: Ramses II, Amun-Ra, Ra-Horakhty and Ptah. Only Ptah, a god linked with the underworld, was positioned so sunlight never reaches him.
  • How early do you need to leave Aswan?

    A standard day trip leaves around 4:00 am; for the Sun Festival, an earlier private departure is recommended so you're inside the temple before sunrise, since the site is busier that morning.
  • What's included in a private Abu Simbel tour?

    Entry fees, a private air-conditioned vehicle and an Egyptologist guide are included; a lunch box is optional and can be added when booking.
  • Is Abu Simbel worth visiting outside the festival dates?

    Yes. The temples are open year-round and just as impressive without the festival crowds, and October to April is generally the most comfortable season to visit.

Whether you time your trip for October 22 or visit on any other day, Abu Simbel is one of the most striking sights in southern Egypt. Plan the early start, book a private departure, and the temple will be waiting in the desert light.
